appraisal_events.evidence: « quand je pourrai je vous ferai chercher » / « ce sera à l'improviste, je ne sais jamais d'avance... Serait-ce possible que je vous fisse chercher le soir quand je serai libre ? »
appraisal_events.explanation: As a staged participant, the narrator unilaterally sets the asymmetric terms of future contact with a tenderly hopeful Albertine, retaining control and emotional leverage over when (or whether) they meet.

status_effects.explanation: He gains relational control over the pace and terms of contact with Albertine, remaining uncommitted while she awaits his convenience.

ambiguities: The candidate list resolves the passage's reference to 'Mme de Stermaria' to the canonical entry 'M. de Stermaria' via alias overlap on 'de Stermaria,' but in context this clearly denotes the woman the narrator hopes to see (elsewhere canonicalized as 'Mlle de Stermaria'), not the male M. de Stermaria; this appears to be an alias-matching artifact rather than a true candidate, and in any case her mention here only restates the motive already captured as evidence in the accepted E1 event, so she was not independently scored.

The narrator's leverage-gain reading is in some tension with the self-aware, slightly abashed tone of 'Je n'osai lui dire'; a stricter reading could treat this as morally ambivalent rather than a clean elevation, so the event is scored with only moderate confidence.
